text:
jacob_cust: Hey team — customer reported streaming responses being truncated mid-event then client reconnects immediately and we see duplicate invoice lines. Happened twice in last hour, req_id=req_8b3f, region=us-west-2. Logs show partial JSON then connection reset. Not sure if proxy or runtime.

maya_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK) and the request_id + approximate times? Also any billing tx ids if available.

jacob_cust: repro below. curl gets initial chunk then stalls, if client retries quickly the platform charges another request. Billing ids: bill_2026_07_22_9 and bill_2026_07_22_10. Timestamp approx 2026-07-22T18:04:12Z.

jacob_cust: ```bash
# reproduce (client that reads very slowly)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/streams?model=small-v1" --no-buffer
```

jacob_cust: node snippet they used to simulate slow reader: ```js
const https = require('https');
const req = https.request(url, {headers: {...}} , res => {
  res.on('data', chunk => {
    // process one byte every 200ms to simulate mobile network
    setTimeout(()=>{/* pretend to process */}, 200);
  });
});
req.end();
```

jacob_cust: server side trace (they pasted): "writev returned -11 errno=EAGAIN, next write after 120ms, then send returned -32 EPIPE, connection reset". Also we see a 200 chunked body but last chunk missing.

maya_support: Thanks — escalating to runtime. @dmitri_eng can you look at req_8b3f? Also billing_ops, customer is requesting temporary credit for duplicated charges.

dmitri_eng: I can dive in. EAGAIN then EPIPE pattern suggests the client stalled reading and kernel tx buffer filled; later either proxy or runtime got SIGPIPE when writing. Two things: (1) platform should avoid double-billing on reconnects where previous stream still active; (2) runtime should detect sustained nonblocking write backlog and fail gracefully rather than let kernel drop/close.

dmitri_eng: Quick ask: can you attach the runtime write logs around req_8b3f (we need timestamps +/- 10s). Also whether this request passed through our edge proxy (yes/no) and which proxy revision.

jacob_cust: edge_proxy: edge-v22, logs attached (pasted excerpt):
```
[18:04:12.123] req_8b3f: chunked-start
[18:04:12.456] req_8b3f: writev(2048)->2048
[18:04:14.678] req_8b3f: writev(8192)->-11 EAGAIN
[18:04:14.800] req_8b3f: retry writev after 120ms
[18:04:15.200] req_8b3f: send()->-32 EPIPE, socket closed by peer
[18:04:15.201] req_8b3f: stream aborted, code=STREAM_ABORTED
```

jacob_cust: Also note: client reconnects at 18:04:16 and immediately gets a fresh request charged. Customer expecting us to correlate reconnect to an in-flight stream and avoid duplicate invoice for quick reconnects.

billing_ops: We can zero-credit the second charge if engineering confirms duplicate processing. Please include billing ids and request ids.

dmitri_eng: Proposed short-term mitigation: detect repeated reconnects from same connection fingerprint within X seconds and treat as a resume attempt (apply idempotency) OR apply a brief soft-window (3s) where we delay billing until stream emits first non-empty event. Long-term: add stream-level write-backpressure monitoring: maintain per-stream outstanding_bytes counter and if > 1MB for > 2s mark stream as slow-consumer and return a 429-style SSE control event and pause generation.

dmitri_eng: Quick config example we can try on prod edge for a few minutes: ```json
{"stream_slow_consumer_soft_limit_bytes":"1048576","stream_slow_consumer_grace_ms":"2000","billing_delay_window_ms":"3000"}
```

maya_support: Is that something you can flip for the affected customer / region right now?

dmitri_eng: I can patch edge-v22 rollout next 10m to enable soft limits for us-west-2. Will monitor errors. Will also add a temporary metric for "slow_consumer_abort_count".

jacob_cust: Appreciate it. Any workaround for customers in meantime? They want to avoid client-side reconnect spam.

dmitri_eng: Recommend client retry backoff (exponential, start 500ms) and to use the Resume-Token we include in stream metadata if available. If the client supports range/resume, prefer that. For mobile SDK: add socket.setTimeout(0) and don't reconnect until you see a final event or explicit abort from server.

billing_ops: I'll hold off automatic refunds until eng confirms duplicate processing. If you confirm, we can issue credit for bill_2026_07_22_10.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-4721 created by maya_support: "slow-client backpressure -> truncated stream -> customer reconnect billing duplicate" assigned to dmitri_eng.

dmitri_eng: Follow-up notes: we saw a couple of similar but not identical cases earlier this week — different proxies but same EAGAIN/EPIPE fingerprint. My plan: 1) enable soft throttle config for us-west-2 for 1 hour, 2) instrument outstanding_bytes metric and alert at 5/min, 3) add billing_delay_window_ms to delay invoice event until client receives first non-empty chunk.

maya_support: Thanks — I'll keep customer updated. jacob_cust, can you confirm when you see the config change and whether it reduces duplicate billing?

jacob_cust: Will test in ~15m and report back. Also, attaching customer's packet capture (pcap) showing client ACKs slowing down before stall.

dmitri_eng: Good evidence. After we flip the soft limit I will also add a temporary rule on the edge to return a small SSE control event: `event: slow_consumer\ndata: {"reason":"slow_client"}` before aborting — that'll help clients detect server-side backpressure and avoid blind reconnects.

maya_support: Copy. Putting customer on hold and will update them after the flip. :thumbsup:

jacob_cust: Verified after 20m — they still get truncated stream but no duplicate invoice so far. Will monitor for 24h. Thanks team.

maya_support: Marking thread resolved for now; will reopen if duplicates reappear.
